findings.observation: This was a two-leg banded squat rather than a single-leg squat; judging the right leg, the knee stayed in line over the toes even at the deepest point, with the band helping keep the knees apart.
cues: Keep your knee pointing over your second toe
Gently push your knees out against the band

findings.observation: Your upper body stayed centred and upright over your feet, with no sideways lean.
cues: Keep your chest tall and centred
Spread your weight evenly through the whole foot

findings.observation: Your hips stayed level throughout the squat.
cues: Keep both hip bones level, like headlights
Squeeze your buttocks gently as you stand up

summary: This video shows a two-leg squat with a band around the knees, not a single-leg squat on the right leg, so it doesn't fully test the surgical leg. Looking at the right leg, the knee lined up well over the toes, the trunk stayed upright and the hips stayed level, with no compensations seen. To check single-leg control, film a single-leg squat on the right leg from the front, 2–3 m away, with your whole body in frame. Talk these observations through with your physio.
